import mir_eval

# Ensure we only use the first two columns (onset, offset) as required by the API
ref_int = ref_intervals[:, :2]
est_int = est_intervals[:, :2]

# Compute the maximum matching based on offset times
matching = mir_eval.transcription.match_note_offsets(ref_int, est_int)

# Verify the contract: maximum matching means the number of matches cannot exceed 
# the number of elements in the smaller of the two sets.
assert isinstance(matching, list), "Expected a list of matched tuples"
assert len(matching) <= min(len(ref_int), len(est_int)), "Number of matches exceeds possible maximum"

# Verify the contract: every reference note is matched against at most one estimated note (and vice versa)
ref_indices = [m[0] for m in matching]
est_indices = [m[1] for m in matching]
assert len(ref_indices) == len(set(ref_indices)), "A reference note was matched more than once"
assert len(est_indices) == len(set(est_indices)), "An estimated note was matched more than once"

print(f"__CHECK__ match_note_offsets {len(matching)}")
